item.title: Tecnologo: NEXT-G FIS-2023-02552 CUP I53C24003120001 “How new genes emerge: exploring a model of novel gene creation following the evolution of wheat” (Univ. PISA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-09 13:00
Institution: Univ. PISA, Pisa
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-06 Genetica, chimica e pedologia agraria e forestale

The NEXT-G project explores how transposons, DNA elements capable of rapidly reorganizing genomes, contribute to the creation of new genes in wheat through the process of exaptation. By applying bioinformatic and genomic approaches, it investigates the evolutionary impact of transposons on the creation of new genes and the mechanisms that drive this process. Focusing on wheat, the project offers new perspectives on the evolution of plant genomes and on adaptation to selective pressures, with particular attention to the early stages of domestication.

Deadline: 2026-12-11 13:00

Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-06 Genetica, chimica e pedologia agraria e forestale

This research aims to investigate how changes in snow cover duration, depth, and distribution influence the physical and chemical properties and functioning of alpine tundra soils. Through multi-year monitoring and investigations along snow persistence gradients, the study will examine relationships among snow regime, soil temperature and moisture, vegetation, and organic matter and nutrient dynamics. The goal is to understand and predict changes in soil properties and functions in response to climate change.
